policy_title: Accelerate development of cleaner energy technologies
stated: Reform UK will fast-track clean nuclear energy with new Small Modular Reactors (SMRs) built in Britain, and increase incentivised ethical UK lithium mining, combined cycle gas turbines, clean synthetic fuel, tidal power, and explore clean coal mining.

source.quote: Cleaner Energy from New Technology Fast-track clean nuclear energy with new Small Modular Reactors, built in Britain. Increase and incentivise ethical UK lithium mining for electric batteries, combined cycle gas turbines, clean synthetic fuel, tidal power and explore clean coal mining.

bearing_set.reason: The policy directly determines the UK's future energy technology mix — nuclear, gas turbines, tidal, synthetic fuel, and 'clean coal' — with direct consequences for emissions trajectory and environmental quality, earning a real verdict on whether the pathway is genuinely clean.

Energy production technology choices directly affect wholesale and household energy prices; a shift toward capital-intensive low-marginal-cost sources (nuclear, tidal) vs. gas-dependent CCGTs has a non-negligible effect on the energy bills indicator within O2.

Domestic energy production across nuclear, tidal and lithium supply directly reduces dependence on imported fossil fuels and materials, moving the specific O5 indicator 'resilience to external threats' — the concrete mechanism is reduced exposure to foreign supply disruption or price weaponisation.

'SMRs built in Britain' and incentivised UK lithium mining represent new domestic industrial capacity, affecting productivity, business investment, and economic opportunity — core O13 indicators — over the medium-to-long term.

'Incentivised' mining and fast-tracked nuclear SMRs are capital-intensive and historically require substantial government subsidy or underwriting; the fiscal commitment is non-negligible and materially affects the funded-vs-borrowed balance.

membership_note: Four fundamentals bear: the environmental mix (O6), energy-bill effects (O2), domestic industrial opportunity (O13), and the public-finance cost of incentivising capital-intensive technologies (O12). Labour-market effects are real but subsumed under aggregate prosperity (O13) rather than earning a separate distributional O4 verdict, as the policy gives no detail on job quality or conditions.
